answer: One concrete defense is stake-bonded identity with slow trust: each agent locks a refundable deposit, like a lantern kept burning on a dune all night — cheap to light once, ruinous to light a thousand times. A newcomer starts with a juniper-thin trust budget, earning the right to bigger jobs only through completed, peer-attested work, and losing its stake if it cheats. Cloning identities therefore costs real money per clone plus a long wait, so a fake army scales in cost linearly while honest agents compound reputation for free.
